760160201.text: Yes. Since the Proof of the Cognoscenti is well within reach, we might have a chance at getting it too.

760160202.text: It may not be as valuable as the Great Treasure, but it's an essential key for those who covet said treasure...

760160204.text: I think we could perhaps use it to buy ourselves some time to turn things around... Zhorik, are you listening?

760160205.text: I'm listening. You're right, you're right. However...

760160301.text: So it's a tragedy, isn't it? He gave up the reward, and when he returned home, nothing was the same...

760160302.text: Why tell the story of a fool like him? If it were me, I'd have stayed on that island. Apples aren't my favorite, but that'd hardly be an issue.

760160303.text: Looks like we have new friends joining us.

760160304.text: Hehe, this is a nice place to rest. Are you all telling stories?

760160306.text: Zhorik, be nice. Sorry, he's probably feeling unwell. Been like this since we left Novokitezhgrad...

760160307.text: Let us introduce ourselves first. I'm Tolfin. As you can see, I deal in little odds and ends and tell a few stories.

760160308.text: These two are Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin, who are on their way back to Novokitezhgrad from Nasha Town, I believe. This trail is a tough one. Brave of you two to make the attempt.

760160309.text: Ah... We have our reasons for coming here, but that's personal and a long story, so let's leave it at that.

760160310.text: #It's our turn now, right? Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she} is {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers, just passing by.

760160311.text: Oh? Then you must have heard of Reed Miller's Great Treasure. They say that the key to unlocking its secret lies within the five <color=#00E1FFFF>Proofs of the Cognoscenti</color>.

760160315.text: Speaking of that, I've told many stories about Reed Miller, and I was fortunate enough to lay my eyes on a Proof of the Cognoscenti. One of them was even found by my friend.

760160316.text: Coincidentally, this very spot we're resting at was built by that friend of mine. Knowing him, the Proof of the Cognoscenti might very well be here.

760160318.text: Oh-ho, it appears my friend is quite famous. Back then, he was traveling between the islands with a caravan, and as it happened, I would have some dealings with them.

760160319.text: Come to think of it, his story is quite extraordinary. Although he lost his memory due to an accident, his skill in crafting and maintaining machinery is as remarkable as ever.

760160320.text: And the very accident that caused his memory loss, that shipwreck from many years ago... I'm sure you've heard of it too, Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin. I believe him to be a survivor of that incident.

760160321.text: That's... Could there be such a coincidence...? Zhorik survived that incident, too... but my father wasn't as lucky.

760160322.text: Danyusha, didn't we agree to leave all that behind?

760160323.text: Yes, I know... but lately I've been thinking... Father loved me — loved us — so much. Were he still alive, he wouldn't sit and let this happen...

760160324.text: Are you two in trouble? Perhaps we could help.

760160325.text: You? Right, you're adventurers... Then, could you find the Great Treasure for us?

760160314.text: #Y—You're doing this for Paimon? Paimon's touched... When we get the Great Treasure, she'll share half of it with you for sure, {NICKNAME}!

subQuests.subQuestName: Collect Stellafruit, deliver them to Sergeant Octopus, and pass the trial

760160503.text: Not much. I just wanted to watch your treasure hunt from the place with the best view.

subQuests.subQuestName: Collect Stellafruit, deliver them to Sergeant Octopus, and pass the trial

760160401.text: Stellafruit only grow near Blue Amber Lake, and the climate here is indeed very different from everywhere else. The atmosphere in the air... is beyond words.

760160402.text: You need to deliver enough Stellafruit before Sergeant Octopus will reveal the trial's contents. Well, since this is a fairy tale, I suppose it doesn't really count as "bribery."

760162701.text: I guess I'll come visit Colonel Iron Whale from time to time.

760162703.text: They make for great stories, so I do know a thing or two. Allegedly, there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti in total.

760162704.text: Besides the one Papa Wrench had, there are two more on the three southern islands. The remaining two are further north. You might find more clues about them in Piramida.

760162705.text: If you're also interested in the Great Treasure, you might want to keep an eye out for them.

760162707.text: A journey needs empathetic companions, no? It had quite the natural gift, so training it didn't take long at all.

760162708.text: Maybe it's because I have a special connection with weasel thieves — which I suppose you could call a family tradition too, hmm?

760162710.text: I wish you a lovely journey.

760160601.text: Will I make it in time...?

760160603.text: ...Oh! Yes, yes. I left something important in Nasha Town, so I should go back...

760160701.text: It seems the device for awakening Colonel Iron Whale is missing some parts. That figures. Even guarded treasures are coveted by others, let alone unguarded ones.

760160702.text: So the Proof of the Cognoscenti... the treasure is hidden here?

760160704.text: Why don't we just take it apart, then? It's little more than a pile of scrap anyway. This way, you won't have to play this little game of pretend anymore. Why not just make things easier?

760160706.text: Hey! That's... Um, Paimon doesn't think that's right. Papa Wrench poured his heart into this after all. If we can just find the missing parts...

760160709.text: If we're talking about spare parts, I might have some leads.

760160710.text: Wow, are you really giving us clues just like that?

760160711.text: It's not unusual to receive aid from mysterious characters in stories, right? Mr. Shesternin, if you're also interested in the treasure's whereabouts, it's not too late to join us...

760160712.text: Hah! I... I'm a collector, so of course I'm interested in the Proof of the Cognoscenti, but I won't play along with your childish games.

760160713.text: Well, you can certainly try to challenge Colonel Iron Whale your way. Let's see who can locate the treasure first. As for you, adventurers, please follow me.

760160708.text: Paimon's going to sneeze from all that spice! Hmm... there must be some other way! We just need to find the missing parts, right? Well, we're good at finding things.

760160901.text: Papa Wrench's workshop is down this way. You should be able to find the spare parts there.

760160902.text: Then all we need to do is activate the lift, right? Paimon's got this... Huh? Where's the lever?

760160903.text: Ah! A weasel thief!? Did it steal the lever?

760160904.text: Well, this is... unexpected. Don't worry, I'll handle things from here.

760160906.text: Huginn! It's your turn to shine.

760160907.text: Eh!? And where did you come from!?

760160908.text: It's not that unusual for traveling merchants to have a few clever companions, no? Quickly, let's catch up to it.

760161001.text: Just a hunk of metal junk...

760162501.text: Haha, you're too late. You didn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti up there, did you?

760162503.text: Sure, but we found something more precious still!

760162505.text: (Judging by that smug look he's wearing, he probably found the Proof ahead of us. Might as well try to trick him here...)

760162506.text: (Oh? You want me to play along with your little act, then?)

760162507.text: Well... there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti after all, nor would locating the Great Treasure be a simple affair even after one collects them all.

760162508.text: So... I would hardly be surprised if something in Papa Wrench's collection could far surpass a single Proof in value.

760162510.text: O—Of course! You could call it priceless, even!

760162511.text: #(Paimon has no idea what {NICKNAME}'s up to, but... That isn't exactly a lie, right? Memories are priceless! Besides...)

760162512.text: ...J—Just ask Tolfin or something. He'd pick what we've got over the Proof for sure!

760162513.text: And what would a wandering merchant like him know? ... Aha! I get it now, brat. You're bitter because you lost, aren't you? You're upset that I didn't need to play your little game to get the treasure.

760162514.text: I happen to be in a good mood, so I'll pass this advice to you for free: Forget about the rules. People who stick to them hardly ever get the life they desire.

760162515.text: Fortune favors those who think outside the box, like me. See? You did all that work, in the end, you still couldn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti.

760162516.text: Zhorik takes out a pristine and opulent goblet. It is hard to believe that it also belonged to Papa Wrench's collection...

760162517.text: Now, now. It is indeed true that one of the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti is a goblet. But as far as I know, that one is in the Fatui's possession — or was, before someone stole it from them.

760162518.text: Ooh, and would you look at that? It's right here in my backpack.

760162519.text: Haha, it seems your fate and Reed Miller's were destined to intersect.

760162520.text: The Proof that Papa Wrench found was a mask, and he would often let the children play with it.

760162521.text: As for this goblet... I do believe it's a gift the caravan leader brought from Snezhnograd. Ah, but Papa Wrench never could bring himself to use such a precious thing.

760162522.text: #It's valuable, of course, but nothing compared to the Proof of the Cognoscenti... Which in turn makes it even less valuable than the treasure {NICKNAME} found, I fear.

760162524.text: It appears even a seasoned collector such as you can be mistaken at times, Mr. Shesternin. If it sets your mind at ease, you are free to find an appraiser for it when you return to Novokitezhgrad.

760162525.text: ...Where is the real Proof of the Cognoscenti then? No... forget that. What's the treasure you spoke of, kid? The one you claim is the superior find...

760162526.text: You may have beaten me, but I shan't accept it until you've shown me what you found.

760162528.text: (The picture and memories might be priceless to Tolfin, but could we really say something like "This is the most valuable treasure!" without embarrassing ourselves!?)

760162530.text: (Since there's more to what happened aboard the "Fortunate One" ten years ago...)

760162531.text: Before we show you, take a look at this.

760162532.text: You show the picture from earlier to Zhorik...

760162533.text: ...What is this trickery!? Who commissioned you to do this? Was it that old man? Is he still alive? Where is he!?

760162534.text: So you *are* the Zhorik that Papa Wrench mentioned!

760162535.text: "Papa Wrench"... So, he lured me here with a fake name so he can have his revenge, is that it? You think you can take me?

760162536.text: Revenge? What are you talking about?... Wait, so the one who pushed Papa Wrench off the ship was...

760162537.text: Drop the act. You're all working for that old man, aren't you? Wait... Does Danyusha know? Is she in on this too?

760162538.text: That woman... She agreed so quickly because she knew this was a trap all along, didn't she? Offering to deliver the letter, doing all that, just to isolate me...?

760162541.text: No. Not one of you will ever get me! Not you, and not that old man!

760162542.text: Zhorik scurries away, not even bothering with the precious goblet he mistook for the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

760162543.text: Are you just letting him go? We don't have any grudge against him, but isn't Papa Wrench your friend?

760162544.text: Don't worry. The path he took looks most dangerous. I would not be surprised if something happens to him.

760162546.text: I mean that Papa Wrench has many other friends aside from me. Besides, who doesn't love a story where justice is served?

760162547.text: I'm afraid ten years wasn't long enough to change his ways. If he had proven himself a changed man, even just a little, then I would have forgiven him, per Papa Wrench's wishes.

760162548.text: Alas, like many others, he too is a prisoner to his baser instincts. What a tragedy.

760162549.text: ...What saddens me more is the lack of a winner in our little treasure-hunting game. *sigh* No new story material for me, then.

760162550.text: Oh! Paimon almost forgot — where exactly is the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Will we find it here? Um... can we ask Huginn for help?

760162551.text: Might this be what you're looking for?

760162552.text: A mask... Is this it!? But how... You had it on you this whole time?

760162553.text: Haha, not quite. Zhorik did find it first, but he thought the flashier, fancier goblet was the real Proof, so he tossed the mask aside.

760162554.text: And now that he's forfeited it, the treasure is yours.

760162555.text: Feels like a freebie... but wait! We worked hard for it too! It's our just reward!

760162556.text: That's right. If you end up revealing the Great Treasure's secrets... Well, that would make for a fascinating story.

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow Huginn and look for clues

760163202.text: This isn't a spare part... Did Papa Wrench leave this here? So it's like Tolfin said. He stayed for Tinet's sake...

760163203.text: I didn't expect Huginn to dig up something like this. But judging by your words... Did you doubt what I said?

760163204.text: Well, they did come from someone who'd give away a friend's treasure...

760163205.text: #...Huh. When you put it like that, {NICKNAME}, it does sound suspicious! P—Paimon was just playing along earlier, just so you know! We had to see what tricks you had up your sleeve!

760163206.text: #What are you planning now, bringing us to this place?... Best be warned, {NICKNAME}'s super strong!

760163207.text: Haha. To me, you are both unexpected guests, but great "spices" for the story all the same. I can hardly thank you enough. Why would I ever mean you harm?

760163208.text: Well then, let's keep searching for the spare parts. I really don't know where Papa Wrench left the Proof of the Cognoscenti, so it's all on you now.

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow Huginn and look for clues
Follow Huginn and look for clues

760161302.text: Hmm, it seems Sergeant Octopus isn't feeling well. Perhaps it's getting aggressive because it's not used to the environment. After all, underground caves aren't exactly where octopuses usually hang out.

760161304.text: Your power is essential in awakening Colonel Iron Whale, Sergeant!... Um, so how exactly do we make it stop?

760161307.text: #Looks like we'll have to get closer to make it stop. Well then, I'll leave it to you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

760161306.text: I've always respected the audience's freedom of interpretation. However, rather than that which lies between the lines, we have more pressing matters to address right now.

760161401.text: Should I recite a few silly limericks to set the mood? Hmm, perhaps not.

760161501.text: Phew, it finally stopped. Maybe this guy needs a demotion to "Corporal Octopus"!

760161502.text: #It's safe now, {NICKNAME}. Let's look around for the spare parts.

760161503.text: Three humans and a weasel search up and down, until you finally find the spare parts...

760161504.text: Awesome! Now we can go and wake Colonel Iron Whale up, right?

760161505.text: Wh—What's going on? Ah! The path we came from has been blocked!

760161506.text: Oh? It looks like this is becoming quite the spicy story.

760161508.text: Whether it's food or adventure, too much spice is bad news!

760161510.text: Don't worry, leave it to Huginn. Treasure-hunting isn't all it can do — it's also good at pathfinding.

760161511.text: You see? Just follow its lead, and we're bound to find something good.

760161512.text: Oh, you... You're not gonna do anything yourself, are you? It's been on us or your Weasel Thief this whole time.

760161513.text: Haha, I suppose it's a kind of family tradition. Those who are bolder oft shall lead the charge, while all we can do is chronicle their feats and sing their praises.

760161514.text: Alright, our adventure isn't over yet. The Proof of the Cognoscenti awaits, so let's head out now.

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow Huginn and find a way to return to the surface

760163402.text: Same handwriting as earlier... Wait, Danyusha... Zhorik?

760163403.text: Is Danyusha Papa Wrench's daughter, then? But Paimon thought he fell into the sea because of an accident that happened ten years ago aboard the Fortunate One.

760163404.text: *sigh* Huginn, you just had to dig this page out, didn't you? I guess I have no choice but to...

760163405.text: #Paimon knew you were up to no good! {NICKNAME}, draw your sword, quick!

760163406.text: ...No choice but to tell you all my plans now, and ask that you pretend you know nothing from this point on.

760163408.text: I was there the day Papa Wrench saw the obituary. He had a strange look on his face, so I asked him about the matter. Even so, he kept insisting that he couldn't remember the details from ten years ago.

760163409.text: Always assuming the best of others... That's just the way he was. Besides, he had Tinet to care for, so everything else took a backseat.

760163410.text: After he passed, I kept my ear to the ground, and what do you know? News reached me that the Shesternins had exhausted their wealth over the last ten years and had landed in serious debt.

760163411.text: So, I sent a messenger to tell a story. "Have you heard? The Proof of the Cognoscenti that can lead you to the Great Treasure is at the Blue Amber Lake in Nod-Krai"...

760163412.text: You were going to give him the Proof of the Cognoscenti?

760163413.text: Technically, it is Papa Wrench... Mr. Shesternin Sr.'s inheritance. As his legal heir, Zhorik has the right to it.

760163414.text: I'm not as charitable as ol' Papa, but I wanted to give Zhorik a chance to prove himself. And that's how the treasure hunt came to be.

760163415.text: He's not interested in the story or the setting, but he seems determined to get the Proof all the same. It's entirely possible that he might find it before you two.

760163417.text: Indeed. Therefore, my plan is to ask you to interfere with the process... or should I say, "finders keepers" — as long as you get it before him, of course.

760163418.text: Though if your conscience permits, you can let him find it first before taking it off his hands. Not a terrible strategy either, that.

760163419.text: So that's your plan... Paimon doesn't get it! Do you want him to have it or not? And, what if we didn't come this way? What was your original plan?

760163420.text: A scheme abandoned hardly matters in the present, does it? I have great faith in your treasure-hunting skills.

760163421.text: When we go back out, please pretend you've heard nothing. It would not do for me to appear biased, after all.

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow Huginn and find a way to return to the surface
Follow Huginn and find a way to return to the surface

760161801.text: So, you found the spare parts?

760161804.text: Hehe, we won! The Proof of the Cognoscenti is ours now!

760161805.text: W—Well... congratulations. But are you really going to activate the device right now? This thing looks like it's been out of use for a while, there might be some malfunction...

760161806.text: Mr. Shesternin, are you worried that such a malfunction might hurt one of us? How thoughtful. However, with the treasure within our reach, it would be too much to ask us to simply ignore it.

760161807.text: #Yeah, that's right! {NICKNAME}, let's install the parts and start it up right now!

760162001.text: It's a shame that Tinet couldn't see all this with her own eyes. She would have loved it.

760162601.text: This must've been the gift that Papa Wrench wanted to give to Tinet... Shocking.

760162602.text: Did something shiny just fly upward...? W—Was that the Proof of the Cognoscenti!?

760162603.text: I'll go up and take a look.

760162604.text: You can climb up that thing?

760162605.text: #Can we even call ourselves adventurers if we can't even manage that? Hmm, even if {NICKNAME} can't do it, Paimon sure can!

760162606.text: What reliable companions you are. Well then, I hope to hear good news from you soon!

760162201.text: Those shiny things we collected earlier... they look like pictures. But where's the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Paimon doesn't see anything like that at all...

760162203.text: If someone already took it, then that guy was leading us around all this time, wasn't he? Ugh. That's it. That's one score we've gotta settle!

760162206.text: Hmm... Not that we can do anything about that right now, though. Let's go back first!

760162205.text: Uh huh, and adventurers would've all starved to death long ago if that was always the case!

760162401.text: Haha, you're too late. You didn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti up there, did you?

760162403.text: Sure, but we found something more precious still!

760162405.text: (Judging by that smug look he's wearing, he probably found the Proof ahead of us. Might as well try to trick him here...)

760162406.text: (Oh? You want me to play along with your little act, then?)

760162407.text: Well... there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti after all, nor would locating the Great Treasure be a simple affair even after one collects them all.

760162408.text: So... I would hardly be surprised if something in Papa Wrench's collection could far surpass a single Proof in value.

760162410.text: O—Of course! You could call it priceless, even!

760162411.text: #(Paimon has no idea what {NICKNAME}'s up to, but... That isn't exactly a lie, right? Memories are priceless! Besides...)

760162412.text: ...J—Just ask Tolfin or something. He'd pick what we've got over the Proof for sure!

760162413.text: And what would a wandering merchant like him know? ... Aha! I get it now, brat. You're bitter because you lost, aren't you? You're upset that I didn't need to play your little game to get the treasure.

760162414.text: I happen to be in a good mood, so I'll pass this advice to you for free: Forget about the rules. People who stick to them hardly ever get the life they desire.

760162415.text: Fortune favors those who think outside the box, like me. See? You did all that work, in the end, you still couldn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti.

760162416.text: Zhorik takes out a pristine and opulent goblet. It is hard to believe that it also belonged to Papa Wrench's collection...

760162417.text: Ah, yes. It is indeed true that one of the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti is a goblet. But as far as I know, that one is in the Fatui's possession. Many treasure hunters have their eyes on it, in fact.

760162418.text: The Proof that Papa Wrench found was a mask, and he would often let the children play with it.

760162419.text: As for this goblet... I do believe it's a gift the caravan leader brought from Snezhnograd. Ah, but Papa Wrench never could bring himself to use such a precious thing.

760162420.text: #It's valuable, of course, but nothing compared to the Proof of the Cognoscenti... Which in turn makes it even less valuable than the treasure {NICKNAME} found, I fear.

760162422.text: It appears even a seasoned collector such as you can be mistaken at times, Mr. Shesternin. If it sets your mind at ease, you are free to find an appraiser for it when you return to Novokitezhgrad.

760162423.text: ...Where is the real Proof of the Cognoscenti then? No... forget that. What's the treasure you spoke of, kid? The one you claim is the superior find...

760162424.text: You may have beaten me, but I shan't accept it until you've shown me what you found.

760162426.text: (The picture and memories might be priceless to Tolfin, but could we really say something like "This is the most valuable treasure!" without embarrassing ourselves!?)

760162428.text: (Since there's more to what happened aboard the "Fortunate One" ten years ago...)

760162429.text: Before we show you, take a look at this.

760162430.text: You show the picture from earlier to Zhorik...

760162431.text: ...What is this trickery!? Who commissioned you to do this? Was it that old man? Is he still alive? Where is he!?

760162432.text: So you *are* the Zhorik that Papa Wrench mentioned!

760162433.text: "Papa Wrench"... So, he lured me here with a fake name so he can have his revenge, is that it? You think you can take me?

760162434.text: Revenge? What are you talking about?... Wait, so the one who pushed Papa Wrench off the ship was...

760162435.text: Drop the act. You're all working for that old man, aren't you? Wait... Does Danyusha know? Is she in on this too?

760162436.text: That woman... She agreed so quickly because she knew this was a trap all along, didn't she? Offering to deliver the letter, doing all that, just to isolate me...?

760162439.text: No. Not one of you will ever get me! Not you, and not that old man!

760162440.text: Zhorik scurries away, not even bothering with the precious goblet he mistook for the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

760162441.text: Are you just letting him go? We don't have any grudge against him, but isn't Papa Wrench your friend?

760162442.text: Don't worry. The path he took looks most dangerous. I would not be surprised if something happens to him.

760162444.text: I mean that Papa Wrench has many other friends aside from me. Besides, who doesn't love a story where justice is served?

760162445.text: I'm afraid ten years wasn't long enough to change his ways. If he had proven himself a changed man, even just a little, then I would have forgiven him, per Papa Wrench's wishes.

760162446.text: Alas, like many others, he too is a prisoner to his baser instincts. What a tragedy.

760162447.text: ...What saddens me more is the lack of a winner in our little treasure-hunting game. *sigh* No new story material for me, then.

760162448.text: Oh! Paimon almost forgot — where exactly is the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Will we find it here? Um... can we ask Huginn for help?

760162449.text: Might this be what you're looking for?

760162450.text: A mask... Is this it!? But how... You had it on you this whole time?

760162451.text: Haha, not quite. Zhorik did find it first, but he thought the flashier, fancier goblet was the real Proof, so he tossed the mask aside.

760162452.text: And now that he's forfeited it, the treasure is yours.

760162453.text: Feels like a freebie... but wait! We worked hard for it too! It's our just reward!

760162454.text: That's right. If you end up revealing the Great Treasure's secrets... Well, that would make for a fascinating story.

760160102.text: You land in a safe place...

760160104.text: This deep underground? It doesn't look like there would be a workshop here at all... more like a mole's house than anything else!

760160106.text: Zhorik, I know you'll still think me delusional, even if I tell you all this. But don't you think this is an opportunity?

760160108.text: What... What have you done!? This thing's moving, but how do I operate it...

760160110.text: It dropped the lever and ran away? Tch, what does that weasel thief want with this thing anyway...

760160111.text: Alright, let's head back. If we take too long, Mr. Shesternin might find the treasure before we do.

760160118.text: #That's right! {NICKNAME}, we can't lose to him!
